PATTERN: When Ned types '2+2' (or '2 reviewers and 2 auditors'), launch 4 agents simultaneously in FOREGROUND (not background) using a single message with 4 Agent tool calls. Two agents do code review (looking for bugs, stale code, test failures), two do architecture/audit (looking for design issues, dead code, inconsistencies). After results come in, ask if he wants to fix all items, then loop again with another 2+2 until all agents agree the codebase is clean.

WHEN: After any significant feature removal or refactor where stale references might linger across many files.

WHY: Multi-pass review catches things a single reviewer misses. Foreground is required because Ned needs results before continuing. The iterative loop (4 rounds this session) is the intended workflow — each pass finds issues the previous missed.

GOTCHA: Ned said 'dude we talked about it' when Claude answered '2+2 = 4' twice — he expects the agent to remember this shorthand. Also: he specifies FOREGROUND explicitly after the first time it ran in background.
